newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE Brent, gas oil charts fly bear flags.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE Brent, gas oil charts fly bear flags.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* The Brent market is likely to move broadly sideways though it will probably sink back rather than make any headway. * Any decline may be as slow as this week's rise with volume low and momentum indicators mostly pegged in neutral territory.

IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures charts are flying more bearish flags today but analysts say momentum is too slow to push the markets convincingly in any direction though most agreed the emphasis remains to the downside.

The upper and low trend lines forming a bearish expanding wedge pattern on the spot month continuation chart for Brent, starting with the July 11 low of $17.32 and high $17.90 and passing through the July 15 17.80 low and July 17 $18.79 high respectively, are seen capping and underpinning the market but with momentum towards the downside.

Analysts said this usually bearish pattern combined with a short term downtrend line stemming from the May 16 high of $20.60 which capped the market at $18.50 on Thursday and topped-off the rallies of Thursday and Friday of last week continued to fuel bear sentiment.
Wee Woon Whai analyst at MMS Singapore said: "In the near term any upside is very limited, hourly charts are looking very overbought and lacking momentum".

"In the medium term there is a choppy but limited downside with very good support around $17.70 (the low of June 20 on the September chart) if this holds there may be a chance for the market to go higher again, perhaps to $19," she added.

However, bear sentiment was further backed up by the formation of a near Doji candlestick on Thursday, where the market opened and closed almost at the same level. This is viewed by those who follow Japanese candlestick charting techniques as a sign of a reversal of a recent trend.
A similar pattern was formed on Monday following last Friday's sharp fall from near $18.70 and the market ticked higher this week.

Analysts said the any decline may be as slow as this week's rise with volume low and momentum indicators mostly pegged in neutral territory. Slow stochastic lines crossed on Wednesday but the recent pattern of trade off these has been for a small decline in prices to fresh lows after a limited rally from a sharp fall.
Independent analyst Elli Gifford said, "$18.50 resistance is proving a bit of a hurdle but some of the downside bias is starting to disappear".
However she said there were several critical resistance points to the upside and expected the market to move sideways to lower.
"The market is likely to move broadly sideways though it will probably sink back rather than make any headway," Gifford said.
Gas oil continued to hold above congested trendline support around $162.50-$163 but the appearance of a Doji Star on the spot month chart, a warning that a prior trend might be ending.

According to Japanese candlestick charting techniques, the emergence of a star after a long, white candle stick (on Wednesday) is usually the sign of a shift from the buyers being in control to a deadlock between the buying and selling forces.
Slow stochastics here to have crossed over and could also be flagging a fall to come, analysts said.
Elli Gifford said she was unimpressed by the market's recent attempts at a clean break above $165 but saw no real resistance until $168.25 and support coming in at $163.25 down to $162.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
